- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via max_scale (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/percent-scale.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57ceb9d6d2af35ebf83d0f8cc396cb612540af74` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6f79c6331a7dda8104209ba4be39b35f5cafda1e` — the merge of head `bb9f927433753b6b83c3faf9476a4683dd1763a7` into base `57ceb9d6d2af35ebf83d0f8cc396cb612540af74`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6f79c6331a7dda8104209ba4be39b35f5cafda1e && git checkout 6f79c6331a7dda8104209ba4be39b35f5cafda1e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57ceb9d6d2af35ebf83d0f8cc396cb612540af74 bb9f927433753b6b83c3faf9476a4683dd1763a7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 57ceb9d6d2af35ebf83d0f8cc396cb612540af74 && git merge --no-ff bb9f927433753b6b83c3faf9476a4683dd1763a7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57ceb9d6d2af35ebf83d0f8cc396cb612540af74
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57ceb9d6d2af35ebf83d0f8cc396cb612540af74` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb9f927433753b6b83c3faf9476a4683dd1763a7`

Isolated at-tier contract review, round 1, for PR #19442 (card #19320), spawned by the `domain:spec` seat-3 PM (seat post #18883); the seat adopts this record verbatim or voids it whole. Every reading below was taken first-hand in a detached worktree at the head above, against merge-base `24162f95` of `origin/main`, after `pnpm install` and a build of the `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/client-react` closures under `os-verify-lock.sh` (34 of 34 tasks, VERDICT command-exit 0). Head asserted via `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/19442/head` at start and again immediately before this post: `bb9f9274` both times. 8 files, +241/−10, matches the PR.

### ① Derived judgments

**J1 — Accept-set delta (Z1): re-derived, agrees.** Real validator from the built dist (`packages/objectql/dist/index.mjs`), 1,950 cells = 5 numeric types × 5 `max` declarations (absent / 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 100) × 6 `scale` values (0 to 5) × 13 place-counts (0 to 12). BEFORE = the same head tree with only `record-validator.ts` restored to its merge-base blob `228585ae` and objectql rebuilt; AFTER = the head blob `2e2d3981`. Result: **1,914 unchanged · 36 ADDED · 0 REMOVED**. The moving classes are exactly `percent max=undefined`, `percent max=0.5`, `percent max=1`, and every added cell is `scale+1` or `scale+2` places (12 per class). `number` / `currency` / `rating` / `slider` at every `max`, and `percent` with `max` 2 or 100, are verdict-identical. Restore proved: blob back to `2e2d3981`, `git status --porcelain` empty, `git diff HEAD` 0 bytes, objectql rebuilt to head (`def.scale + 2` present in the dist once). Judgment: the widening is real, bounded to fraction-stored percent, and the narrowing arm is empty — CORRECT.

**J2 — The Clause-② arm, and the ruling's `no` (Z1).** I agree with the seat that `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the declaration this diff owes, and I do not think the ruling's `no` should stand as the routing input: (i) the ruling's own Execution parenthetical concedes "accept set widens for stored fractions only by the declared derivation", and AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist step 3 makes `no (widening)` a malformed pair, so that line cannot carry the arm it describes; (ii) `contract-review.md` calls the declaration provisional and routing-only, and says an unsure claim goes `yes`; (iii) `yes` is what forces at least `minor`, which is what the changeset declares. This is a routing difference, not a re-adjudication of ruling B: the ruling's substantive letter (both halves) is implemented as written. No maintainer trip is needed on this point; the discrepancy is recorded here.

**J3 — The code does what ruling B says (Z2).** `record-validator.ts` lines 810 to 812: `allowed` is `def.scale + 2` when `t === 'percent'` and `percentScaleOf(def) === 'fraction'`, otherwise `def.scale`; the refusal fires when `actual` exceeds `allowed`, inside the existing well-formedness guard (`Number.isInteger(def.scale)`, `def.scale` at or above 0), after `invalid_number` / `min_value` / `max_value`. The split is read from the spec's `percentScaleOf` (`max` above 1 ⇒ whole), not re-derived. Premise probe reproduced through the real dist. BEFORE: fraction `scale:2` 0.1234 ⇒ `max_scale {scale:2, actual:4}`; 0.123 ⇒ `{2,3}`; `scale:3` 0.33333 ⇒ `{3,5}`; `scale:0` 0.33 ⇒ `{0,2}` — all four refused, as the card claimed. Lit control, same instrument, same run: 0.12 and 0.5 ACCEPTED; `max:1` with 5 ⇒ `max_value {max:1}`; `min:0` with −0.5 ⇒ `min_value {min:0}`; `'abc'` ⇒ `invalid_number`; `number` / `currency` / `slider` / `rating` at `scale:2` refuse 1.234 with `{2,3}`. AFTER: the four ruling-accept cases accept; 0.12345 refused `max_scale {scale:4, actual:5}` with message "Rate must have at most 4 decimal places (got 5)"; whole `max:100 scale:2`: 12.34 accepts, 12.345 refused `{2,3}` — unchanged; every lit-control and other-type reading is byte-identical before and after. The formula seam is untouched by construction (`roundFormulaValue` runs on `type === 'formula'` plan entries only, and `percentScaleOf` answers `undefined` off `percent`), and the DDL side already maps `percent` to `EXACT` (`numeric-column-representation.ts` line 232), so the widened accept set reaches the column without rounding. CORRECT.

**J4 — The pin discriminates (Z3).** HEAD baseline on the one file: 108 of 108 pass, the #19320 block 13 of 13. Ablation M0 through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor `? def.scale + 2` replaced by `? def.scale + 0`: anchor ×1 to ×0, blob `2e2d3981` to `7b082941`, **8 failed / 100 passed (108)** — reproduces the dev's reading exactly, and the 8 are the 8 the dev named (worked example, scale+1 ceiling, applied-allowance envelope, `percentScaleOf` split, scale:0, 33.333%, string and exponent forms, localized message). Restore proved by the tool: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty. The 5 survivors are exactly the 5 the dev declared non-discriminating, and each is anti-vacuity rather than dead weight, shown by planting a different mutation and watching it fire: M1 `? Infinity` (scale no longer enforced on fraction percent) ⇒ the **scale+3 refusal** fails (6 failed in the file); M2b `t === 'percent' && true` (fraction/whole split dropped) ⇒ the **whole-percent pin** and the split pin fail (2); M3 `: def.scale;` to `: def.scale + 2;` (blanket +2) ⇒ the **other-numeric-types controls** fail, with whole-percent and split (9); M4 skip `min` on percent ⇒ the **other-refusal-reasons control** fails (1); M5 default `scale` to 2 when undeclared ⇒ the **no-declared-scale control** fails (2). For the record: my first M2 plant was **void** in exactly the way the dev's first attempt was — replacement `t === 'percent'` is a prefix of the anchor, its count read ×2 to ×2, and the tool refused before running anything — recorded, then re-planted with a non-prefix replacement. After every leg the file's blob is `2e2d3981d29a7830c293a947b63de3dda1410230`, byte-identical to the shipped file at head, so nothing landed on the production file after the pin was proved able to fail. CORRECT.

**J5 — The docblock half and the generated pages (Z4).** `FieldSchema.scale`'s `.describe()` now states both meanings in one sentence: what the number counts on `percent` (displayed percentage-point decimals, `scale: 2` means 12.34%), what it permits in storage (fraction ⇒ `scale + 2`, whole ⇒ exactly `scale`, every other numeric type ⇒ exactly `scale`), and keeps the 0 to 100 platform ceiling. `percent-scale.ts` gains a pointer, not a second copy. Regeneration: `git diff 24162f95..HEAD -- content/docs` touches exactly `references/data/field.mdx` (+1/−1), `references/data/object.mdx` (+2/−2), `references/system/migration.mdx` (+2/−2) — the 7 occurrences of the `FieldSchema` table — and nothing else. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` on the head tree: **exit 0, all 15 artifacts up to date**, with `check:docs content/docs/references/**` and `check:authorable-surface` each named green, so the three pages are byte-equal to what the generator produces from source; a hand-edit would have reddened `check:docs`. CORRECT.

**J6 — The refusal envelope reports the APPLIED allowance (Z4, the seat's ruling tested).** I judge the call correct, on published contract text rather than taste: `FieldErrorSchema.constraint` is described as "The constraint that was violated, as discrete values", and its docblock says those values "are what the message templates interpolate". The `max_scale` template renders `{{scale}}` and `{{actual}}` verbatim in all four locales, so `{scale: 2, actual: 5}` on a field that accepts 4 would interpolate a sentence that is false, and `actual` counts places in the number as written, so `scale` must sit on the same axis to be the constraint that was violated. Premise re-measured for `constraint.scale` / `constraint?.scale` readers: objectstack at head **0 files** (lit control: `max_scale` in 16 files); objectui at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `53ded82b`: 0, and `max_scale` is also 0 there, so that zero proves nothing by itself; objectui `origin/main` `98178b20`: 0, with `max_scale` in 2 files (`PercentField.tsx` and its `storedScale-9810` test, docblock prose only) as the lit control; the only non-test `.constraint` reader in the other packages is `service-settings` forwarding its own breach. ⛔ `cloud` / `objectos` / `hotcrm` NOT MEASURED, outside scope. Widening-safe: no consumer found that echoes `constraint.scale` as the raw declaration. CORRECT, and pinned (`constraint: { scale: 4, actual: 5 }`).

**J7 — Public surface.** No export added, removed or retyped in `@objectstack/objectql` or `@objectstack/spec` (`check:api-surface` green; `authorable-surface.base.json` unmoved); the accept set is the only thing that widened. `dispatch-gates --tier`: no path-derived mandate, no governed-surface path in the file list, 251 changed lines against the 5,000 human-merge threshold.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/19320-percent-storage-scale-derivation.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`, carrying `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on a line of its own. Consistent: `yes` takes at least `minor`; a behaviour widening with an empty narrowing arm is `minor`, not `major`; nothing is removed or renamed, so no migration text is owed and no ADR-0087 disposition marker applies. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. The PR body's line 3 reads bare `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (the describing near-miss the dev measured was repaired by the seat) and `--pair` reads the card's claim as `DECLARED yes (arm: widening)`. CONSISTENT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag — the docblock half lay outside the dispatched boundary** (`field.zod.ts` plus three regenerated pages): authorized by the seat as option A, landed on the same branch, and the ruling names that surface itself. Resolved.
- **Dev flag — Clause-② arm against the ruling's `no`**: answered in J2. `yes (widening)` stands; routing, not re-adjudication.
- **Dev flag — envelope reports the applied allowance**: answered in J6. Correct, pinned.
- **Acceptance note — the `max_scale` message describes the stored fraction, not the typed number.** Agreed it is not a defect: the sentence is now internally true and coherent with the envelope; whether a percent-specific sentence is wanted is a display decision for the ruling's author. Carried here, not escalated.
- **Acceptance note — `numeric-column-representation.ts` needs no change**: agreed; `percent: EXACT` already holds both storage scales and its own comment anticipates `0.33333`.
- **Dev observation — `check:skill-examples` spells a prerequisite refusal as `exit 1`**: confirmed at source — `refuse()` and `fail()` both `process.exit(1)` in `packages/spec/scripts/check-skill-examples.ts`, and its docblock states the shared code is deliberate. It is a real classification hazard for `--ran` reconciliation (a refusal reads as red). It reached its real verdict on my sweep (see Gates), so the refusal was not observed here. Recommend the seat file it as a gate finding; not the dev's write and not mine.
- **Carrier state, a seat write and not this review's**: `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19442` read **exit 4, row C3** before this post — the card declares `Clause-②: yes` while NEITHER carrier carries `needs:contract-review`, and both event streams show the gate was never hung. The claim comment says both carriers carry it; they do not. The post-post reading goes in the seat report.

### Gates and CI

**Gate family (Z5), re-derived and re-run.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` from the head worktree derives **111** commands from the real 8 changed paths against merge-base `24162f95` (the first round's 63 was the four-file surface; 111 is the widened one — the dev's "a clue, not a spec" is the right reading). All 111 were run on the pristine head tree (`git status --porcelain` empty before the sweep, refused otherwise), each under `timeout 600`, the true exit captured before any pipe into `ran.list` in the tool's own `:: exit N` form. Result: **111 run · 107 exit 0 · 0 red · 4 non-zero, none a finding**: `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` exit 3 (its positive control is pinned to `621a4876`, unreachable in this shallow clone), `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 (28 packages have no `dist/`, "nothing was measured"), `check:type-check-debt` exit 3 (needs the workspace closure built), `check-engine-split-ratio.mjs --days 90` exit 2 (the shallow clone's oldest visible commit, 2026-08-31, sits inside the 90-day window, so it refuses rather than print a plausible wrong ratio). No exit 124, no signal exit. `dispatch-gates --ran ran.list --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: **111 derived, 108 run, 3 NOT-MEASURED (all three DERIVED from the recorded exit 3), 0 UNRUN, true exit 0.** Disclosure (a) confirmed: the reconciler classifies the exit-2 refusal as "run" because 2 is neither `EXIT_PREREQUISITE_NOT_MET` nor a kill code, yet that gate measured nothing — reporting it as NOT MEASURED against the reconciler is the honest reading, so this review's count is **4 NOT MEASURED**, not 3. Disclosure (b) confirmed at source: `packages/spec/scripts/check-skill-examples.ts` spells `refuse()` and `fail()` as the same `process.exit(1)`, deliberately, so a `--ran` record cannot tell a prerequisite refusal from a finding; on this sweep the gate reached its real verdict — **exit 0, 258 prose examples across 106 files and 3 surfaces, spec-source TSDoc included** — because the `@objectstack/client-react` closure was built before the sweep, so the refusal itself was not observed here. The dev's repaired red, `check:error-code-casing`, is exit 0 on this head. Each unmeasured family is measured by CI on this head: `check-plugin-teardown-shape` inside `Lint & Repo Gates`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` inside `Build Core`, `check:type-check-debt` inside `Type Check · debt ledger` — all `success`; `check-engine-split-ratio --days 90` is not a per-PR step I could find in `lint.yml` or `ci.yml` (only its `--self-test` runs there, and that is exit 0 on this sweep).

**CI on `bb9f9274`, check-runs per name, newest-run-wins**: 49 raw runs, 35 distinct names — 31 `success`, 4 `skipped` (Auto Label, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in), **0 failure, 0 cancelled**. The required seven — Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard — all `completed/success`. Failures on the two earlier shas are not on this head and are not reported.

**Render risk (Z6), measured as far as a checkout allows.** The three regenerated pages were parsed with the docs site's own `remark-parse` + `remark-gfm`: every `scale` row is a well-formed 4-cell row on all 7 occurrences; the new cell is 833 text characters with 12 inline-code spans and no angle brackets, braces or unescaped pipes. The same `FieldSchema` table already carries a longer cell (`readonly`, about 942 raw characters) and neighbours of 300 to 450 (`min`, `max`, `useGrouping`, `rows`), so the row sits inside the page's existing envelope. `Build Docs` — the production `vercel.json` buildCommand under `TURBO_FORCE` — is `success` on this head, so the MDX compiles and the page builds. Judgment: acceptable as rendered markdown; the one stylistic cost is a long prose sentence in a cell, which this page already accepts on `valueDomain`, `readonly`, `min` and `max`. The visual wrap in a browser is NOT MEASURED.

### NOT MEASURED

- `cloud` / `objectos` / `hotcrm` for `constraint.scale` consumers — outside scope.
- Browser rendering of the regenerated table cell — only the parse and `Build Docs` were measured.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt` (whole-workspace build not done locally) and `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` (pinned commit unreachable) — exit 3 here; measured green by CI on this head in the jobs named above.
- `check-engine-split-ratio.mjs --days 90` — exit 2, shallow clone; not a per-PR CI step as far as the workflows show.
- The `exit 1` prerequisite refusal of `check:skill-examples` — its spelling was confirmed at source, not observed on this run.
